source: live published KnownIssue rows plus AffiliateClick aggregates

records.title: R1T / R1S Charge Port Motor / Door Failure
records.description: Multiple owner reports of the charge port door motor failing — door refuses to open via app/touchscreen/button, sometimes stuck open after charge session. Cold weather amplifies failure rate. Rivian replaces under warranty; some early VINs received recall for related door-latch behavior.
records.solution: Service center charge port assembly replacement under warranty. Out-of-warranty $400-$700. Owners can sometimes manually push the door (gently) to free a stuck door — emergency release procedure in owner's manual.

records.title: Driver seat belt pretensioner cable damage from driver sitting on buckled belt (Recall 25V-816)
records.description: NHTSA recall 25V-816 affects ~34,824 EDVs built Dec 2021 - Nov 2025. Repeated driver misuse (sitting on a buckled belt that is tucked under the driver) abrades and damages the pretensioner cable, which may fail to adequately restrain the occupant in a crash. NHTSA opened the probe Sept 2025; Rivian voluntarily recalled in Nov 2025. OTA software now detects misuse and chimes.
records.solution: Free dealer/mobile-service inspection and replacement of the pretensioner cable under recall 25V-816. Install OTA update with seat-belt misuse detection. Train drivers to buckle the belt across the body, not under them.
symptoms: Frayed or kinked seat belt cable visible at the B-pillar
Belt does not pre-tension during hard braking
Driver habitually buckles belt and then sits on top of it

citations.title: Rivian Recalls Nearly 35,000 Electric Delivery Vans Over Seat Belt Issue (WardsAuto)

records.title: Front upper control arm / steering knuckle fastener under-torqued (Recall 22V-744)
records.description: Subset of 2022 EDVs built Dec 10, 2021 - Sept 27, 2022 may have an improperly torqued fastener joining the front upper control arm to the steering knuckle. Symptoms include excessive NVH from the front suspension and changed steering feel. In rare cases the joint can separate, causing loss of vehicle control. Shared campaign with R1T/R1S; Rivian internal number FSAM-997.
records.solution: Free recall inspection at Rivian Service (FSAM-997 / NHTSA 22V-744). Tech torques fastener to spec; replaces knuckle/control arm if wear is found. Do not drive if a clunk is felt over bumps - request mobile service.

records.title: Thermal events / vehicle fires while parked at depot chargers in extreme heat
records.description: Multiple incidents of EDVs catching fire at Amazon depots while parked at L2 chargers. Most-publicized event: 3 EDVs ignited on July 1, 2024 at a Houston fulfillment center on a ~100F day (plugged in but not actively charging). Earlier incident at a Salt Lake City depot in Aug 2023. Rivian states the HV battery was NOT the initiator; investigators suspect the charger / EVSE or 12V system in high ambient heat. No injuries, but fire can spread to adjacent parked vans.
records.solution: If your fleet operates EDVs at depot chargers in hot climates, space vans apart, monitor chargers for damage/heat, and contact Rivian commercial support. Per Rivian, the HV battery was not the initiator in the Houston incident; root cause remains officially undetermined as of the cited reporting. Do not assume EVSE/12V causation - investigations by Amazon's third-party investigator and Rivian are ongoing.
symptoms: Smoke or flames from vans parked at L2 depot chargers in high ambient heat (~100F+)
Fire propagation to adjacent parked EDVs
Charger circuit panel damage at affected stalls

records.title: R1S Third-Row Creaks / Folding Mechanism Issues
records.description: R1S third-row seats commonly creak and squeak over bumps, with some owners reporting the powered folding mechanism getting stuck mid-deploy. Plastic-on-plastic and metal-on-plastic contact points are usually the source. Rivian has applied service bulletins addressing common creak points.
records.solution: Service center can apply TSB-recommended bushings/dampers — typically covered under warranty. Out-of-warranty repairs $150-$400. Some owners DIY with felt/foam tape at known contact points.

records.title: Early R1T Upper Control Arm Corrosion (Salt-Belt)
records.description: Early R1T owners in salt-belt regions (US Northeast/Midwest, Canada) report surprising rapid surface corrosion on the upper control arms — bare metal exposed at welds, bushings showing rust through finish. Rivian made running production changes around mid-2023. Affected cars eligible for inspection.
records.solution: Schedule Rivian service inspection — many cars have been replaced under warranty for early-onset corrosion. Annual underbody wash strongly recommended. Aftermarket undercoating shops can treat at owner expense ($400-$800).

records.title: R1T Frunk Auto-Close Finger Pinch Recall (22V-176)
records.description: Rivian issued a software action in 2022 covering R1T vehicles for a frunk (front trunk) auto-close obstacle-detection issue — the powered frunk could close on fingers when the detection didn't trigger correctly. Software-only remedy via OTA. Check the official Rivian recall lookup for current campaign status applicable to your VIN.
records.solution: Software update via OTA was the remedy. Confirm VIN via rivian.com/support/article/recall-information or the NHTSA recall lookup. If older software, plug in at home to download the OTA.

records.title: R1T / R1S 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain (Gear Guard, Cellular Modem)
records.description: R1T and R1S report 12V drain after long parking — particularly with Gear Guard (cabin/exterior camera surveillance) enabled, which keeps cellular modem and cameras active. Owners report dead 12V in 7-14 days without Gear Guard, faster with it. Multiple OTA updates have improved parasitic draw but not eliminated.
records.solution: Update to latest software. Disable Gear Guard for long parking. Use a 12V battery maintainer for storage stretches over 2 weeks. AGM 12V replacement under warranty for early failures; out-of-warranty ~$250-$400.

records.title: R1T / R1S Brake Lights Stay On in "Bench Mode" (Recall 23V-159)
records.description: Rivian has issued multiple software actions across 2023 covering lighting/visibility issues on R1T and R1S — including brake-light behavior in various drive modes (Conserve, Wade) that could keep brake lights illuminated when not appropriate. Multiple campaigns; consult Rivian recall lookup for status applicable to your VIN.
records.solution: OTA updates apply the fixes automatically. Confirm via rivian.com/support/article/recall-information or NHTSA recall lookup against your VIN. Keep car connected to Wi-Fi at home to receive OTAs promptly.

records.title: R1T / R1S Quad-Motor Front Drive Unit Failures
records.description: Early-production Quad-Motor R1T and R1S (2022-2023) have documented front drive unit failures — typically presenting as a grinding/whining noise, vehicle warnings about drive system, or sudden loss of front-axle drive. Rivian has replaced many under warranty; reports cluster around 20,000-40,000 miles. Quad-Motor architecture (separate motors per wheel) means a single DU failure leaves three working motors but with warning lights.
records.solution: Rivian warranty replacement is the standard fix (8 yr / 175,000 mi powertrain). Document any noise or warning promptly. Out-of-warranty drive unit replacement is dealer-only and likely $4,000-$8,000 per unit.

records.title: R1T / R1S Infotainment Freezes + Black-Screen Reboots
records.description: R1T and R1S center display and driver display can freeze, reboot mid-drive, or go black entirely — particularly during cellular handoffs (entering/leaving tunnel), after wake from sleep, or during OTA installation. Loss of driver display means losing speed/range readout in motion (workaround: use HUD if equipped or phone). Multiple OTA releases have improved but not eliminated.
records.solution: Hard reset: hold both scroll wheels on steering wheel 10+ seconds. Severe cases require service center module replacement. Stay on latest software (OTA). Some owners disable Gear Guard to reduce modem-related reboots.

records.title: R1T / R1S Front Seat Belt Anchor Recall (22V-641, 207 Vehicles)
records.description: NHTSA recall 22V-641 covers approximately 198 R1T and 9 R1S model year 2022 vehicles produced between January 28, 2022 and August 8, 2022 for front seat belt anchors inadequately attached to the B-pillar. Improperly secured anchors may not restrain occupants during a crash. Owners may notice rattling noises from the height-adjuster area of the B-pillar if a bolt is loose.
records.solution: Free recall remedy via Rivian Mobile Service Technician or Rivian Service Center — anchor inspection and proper securing. ~1 hour. Schedule via 1-855-748-4265. Confirm VIN against 22V-641.

records.title: 400V architecture limits DC fast-charging speed vs 800V competitors
records.description: Rivian chose a 400-volt electrical architecture (353.3V nominal: 8 strings of 96 LG 4695 cells) for the R2, vs 800V used by Hyundai Ioniq 5, Kia EV6, Porsche Macan EV, BMW iX3, Volvo EX60. EPA filings list a peak DC rate of 217 kW, but independent carwow testing on Rivian Adventure Network measured a real-world peak of 181-190 kW that dropped to ~150 kW by 50% SOC and ~53 kW by 83% SOC. Rivian advertises 10-80% in 29 min on the 87.9 kWh usable (94 kWh gross) NMCA pack. Owners road-tripping behind 800V vehicles will spend roughly 10 extra minutes per stop. CEO Scaringe defended the trade-off citing R1 fleet data of ~10 DC sessions/year/owner, prioritizing range and cost per kWh over peak fast-charge speed.
records.solution: Charge at home on Level 2 whenever possible (Rivian designed around this). On road trips, stop at ~20% and unplug at 60-70% to stay in the high-power part of the curve rather than waiting through the taper. Use Rivian Adventure Network for best curve adherence.
symptoms: Peak DC fast-charge rate ~190 kW, not class-leading
Aggressive taper above 50% SOC during long trips
10-80% time ~29 min vs ~20 min on 800V rivals
Slower road-trip cadence vs Ioniq 5 / Macan EV

records.title: Electronic door handles — rear-seat manual emergency release is hidden behind trim
records.description: The R2 carries over Rivian's e-latch door system: no mechanical linkage between the interior handle/button and the latch. Rivian moved the rear-door manual release forward into the grab-handle area (an improvement over the R1's door-panel location), but the cable is still hidden behind a small plastic cover that must be popped out to access — criticized by safety reviewers (Carscoops, autoevolution, InsideEVs, TechCrunch) as non-intuitive in a power-loss or fire emergency, especially for rear-seat children. The R2's electromechanical latch system does automatically unlock doors when a crash is detected, with fully redundant HV/12V power, per Rivian design chief Jeff Hammoud.
records.solution: Owners must demonstrate the hidden rear manual release to every passenger before driving — show how to pop the trim piece and pull the cable. Keep a window-breaker tool in the cabin. No Rivian-issued recall or service fix as of June 2026.
symptoms: Rear-seat occupants cannot intuitively find manual door release
Plastic trim must be popped/removed to reach release cable
Risk of entrapment after 12V power loss or fire if occupants are unfamiliar with location
Children may be unable to operate manual rear release
